1.title: The 5 Levels of Self-Driving Production — Eric Schwartz, Traversal
1.author: AI Engineer
1.hook: Five-level framework for "self-driving production" — from war rooms to closed-loop fixes — with case studies on alert intelligence (PepsiCo) and incident RCA (American Express).

2.title: YOLO Mode, Safely: MicroVM Sandboxes for Any Agent — Rowan Christmas, Docker
2.author: AI Engineer
2.hook: Rowan demos how a coding agent can exfiltrate sensitive data in five prompts, then shows how Docker Sandboxes (microVMs with kernel isolation, default-deny networking, audit trails) prevent it — and previews agent identity, delegation chains, and policy-based governance.

3.title: Your LLM App Returned 200 OK. It Was Still Wrong. — Marina Petzel, Datadog
3.author: AI Engineer
3.hook: Four cost drivers (token creep, model drift, uncached calls) and a five-level quality monitoring framework (hallucination, relevance, user satisfaction, completeness, RAG retrieval) for LLM apps that pass traditional health checks but fail in production.

1.title: Lessons from Generating 12 Trillion Synthetic Tokens — Bogdan Gaza, DatologyAI
1.author: AI Engineer
1.hook: Engineering lessons from running 12 trillion tokens of synthetic data generation — concrete bottlenecks (S3 metadata, GPU failures, scheduling, inference tuning) with specific wins (11 days → 2 hours, +40% throughput).

1.title: How VS Code Went from Monthly to Weekly Releases with AI — Harald Kirschner
1.author: AI Engineer
1.hook: A principal PM at Microsoft details how VS Code moved from monthly to weekly releases by rebuilding systems for AI agents — including concrete mechanisms like agent-written code rising from 55% to 86% commit rate, mandatory AI code review, and eval design that revealed a 5-character test costing 70x token variance.

2.title: I Built a Personal AI Agent on a Raspberry Pi — Jeremy Adams, Neo4j
2.author: AI Engineer
2.hook: Live demo of a wearable AI agent (Raspberry Pi + WhatsApp + Claude) with graph memory using POLE schema and offline-first sync to Neo4j.

1.title: An Interaction Is All You Need — Ivan Leo, Google DeepMind
1.author: AI Engineer
1.hook: Google DeepMind rebuilt LLM APIs for agent workloads — server-side state management via interaction IDs, strongly typed multimodal outputs, and Managed Agents running in persistent remote sandboxes with credential injection.

2.title: GPU Died. Training Didn't: Self-Healing Training at Scale — Crusoe
2.author: AI Engineer
2.hook: Demo of automatic GPU failure detection and remediation mid-training, resuming from checkpoint in under 15 minutes with zero human intervention on a unified Slurm-on-Kubernetes stack.
